Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

transitmattr 0.3.0

Breaking changes

  • tm_git_id() has been removed. The API no longer has a /api/git_id endpoint.

  • tm_scheduled_service() now requires route_id, as the API does.

  • Results have R types instead of the API’s strings: times are POSIXct date-times in Eastern time (America/New_York), dates are Dates, and the time of day in $aggregate_travel_times_v2()‘s by_time is an hms. Headway direction is an integer, like the other events’. Column names are unchanged. Code that parsed these columns itself, e.g. with as.POSIXct() or as.Date(), still works but no longer needs to.

  • Errors have transitmattr’s own classes, such as transitmattr_not_found and transitmattr_range_too_long (see ?transitmattr_errors), and their messages include the API’s explanation. They keep httr2’s httr2_http_<status> classes too.

  • A 500 response is no longer retried; the API also sends one for bad requests.

New features

  • New endpoints:

    • tm_bus_query(route)$trip_metrics(): trips delivered, miles, and speeds for a bus route, optionally for one time_band or day_type.
    • tm_cr_query(route)$trip_metrics(): commuter rail fleet mix.
    • tm_cr_query(route)$reliability() and tm_reliability(): on-time performance for commuter rail or The RIDE.
    • tm_cr_query(route)$scorecard(): a commuter rail schedule measured against Regional Rail standards.
    • tm_bus_speed_leaderboard(): the slowest bus routes over a date range.
    • tm_weather(): hourly weather in downtown Boston.
    • $aggregate_travel_times_v2() on rapid transit and commuter rail queries: travel time statistics by date and by time of day.

  • $headways(), $dwells(), and $travel_times() fetch every day in $date_range() when no single date is set, several days at a time, and return one data frame. tm_alerts() takes an end_date. Set options(transitmattr.max_concurrency = n) to change how many requests are in flight at once (default 8).

  • The $trip_metrics() methods accept ranges longer than the API’s limit of 150 days, weeks, or months, by fetching them in pieces.

  • Requests that time out, fail to connect, or get a 429, 502, 503, or 504 are retried up to three times with exponential backoff, waiting as long as a Retry-After header asks.

  • agg arguments accept "monthly" wherever the API does ($trip_metrics(), $service_hours(), $scheduled_service()), and values the API doesn’t accept are rejected before a request is sent.

Bug fixes

  • tm_rt_query(line)$scheduled_service() returned an empty data frame. It now returns the same list as tm_scheduled_service().

  • tm_healthcheck() returns the failing checks when the API reports a failure, instead of raising an HTTP 500 error.

  • tm_stops() percent-encodes route IDs, so combined bus routes such as "SL4/SL5" work.

Internals

  • Requests now go through a client generated from the API’s OpenAPI spec with OpenAPI Generator (R/generated-*.R). The spec is pinned in spec/openapi.json; a weekly GitHub Actions workflow syncs it from upstream, regenerates the client, and opens a pull request.

  • The user agent now reports the installed package version.

  • DESCRIPTION now requires R 4.1 and httr2 1.1.1, which the package already needed: httr2 requires R 4.1, and parallel requests need httr2 1.1.1.

  • A test keeps a snapshot of every response model’s fields, so a spec sync that adds, removes, or renames a field fails until someone checks whether .tm_conversions in R/convert.R needs updating.

transitmattr 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • All mode-specific data functions (tm_headways(), tm_dwells(), tm_travel_times(), tm_ridership(), tm_trip_metrics(), tm_line_delays(), tm_service_hours(), tm_speed_restrictions(), tm_aggregate_headways(), tm_aggregate_dwells(), tm_aggregate_travel_times(), tm_aggregate_travel_times2()) have been removed. Use the new query builder interface instead (see below).

  • tm_time_predictions() now requires a route_id argument.

  • All data-fetching functions previously returned a list of records. Query builder terminal methods now return a data.frame directly, so bind_rows() or do.call(rbind, ...) conversions are no longer needed.

New query builder interface

Data is now fetched through mode-specific R6 query objects. Each object is created with a constructor, configured by chaining builder methods, and activated by a terminal method:

  • tm_rt_query(line) — rapid transit (Red, Orange, Blue, Green, Mattapan)
  • tm_bus_query(route) — bus routes
  • tm_cr_query(route) — commuter rail routes
  • tm_ferry_query(route) — ferry routes

Builder methods (return the object invisibly for chaining): $stop(), $from_stop(), $to_stop(), $direction(), $date(), $date_range()

Discovery methods: $stations() and $directions() return data frames of available stops/directions without hitting the data API.

Terminal methods (return a data.frame): $headways(), $dwells(), $travel_times(), $aggregate_headways(), $aggregate_dwells(), $aggregate_travel_times(), $ridership(), $trip_metrics(), $line_delays(), $service_hours(), $scheduled_service(), $speed_restrictions()

Commuter rail and ferry terminus stations now emit a warning when selected via $stop(), $from_stop(), or $to_stop(), as stop IDs may be missing in one direction.

New functions

  • tm_bus_routes() — returns a sorted character vector of all supported bus route IDs (local lookup, no API call).
  • tm_cr_routes() — same for commuter rail routes.
  • tm_ferry_routes() — same for ferry routes.
